mainTopic: When prohibitions stack for a כהן גדול (separate bodies, איסור מוסיף, איסור חל על איסור), and how a woman becomes a חללה
overview: This amud deals with a כהן גדול and the women forbidden to him, and asks when he gets more than one set of מלקות. First the גמרא shows that one act with a woman widowed three times brings only one punishment, because separate bodies are needed, not just separate names. Next it explains why a woman who became an אלמנה, then a גרושה, then a חללה, then a זונה brings a punishment for each. רבא says this תנא holds איסור מוסיף: a new prohibition takes effect when it adds a new restriction. A ברייתא taught before רב ששת says a כהן גדול is not liable for אלמנה with his widowed sister. The גמרא debates whether that ברייתא follows רבי שמעון or the רבנן. אביי then rules that a woman becomes a חללה only through a prohibition of כהונה, and רבא brings the ברייתא that is the source. רב אשי begins to draw a practical result about a כהן who lives with his sister, and his statement continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Three different widows would mean three punishments
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that 'many widows' means three different women, because three women are separate bodies and separate prohibitions.
steps.simpleTranslation: But three different women are separate bodies, and each one is a separate forbidden 'name'! So he should be punished for each one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the first suggestion, that the case is a כהן גדול who was with three different widows. Three different widows should clearly bring three punishments, not one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two separate things can each split a punishment into several: separate people (גופין) and separate prohibitions (שמות). With three different widows, both are present. So the ruling 'only one punishment' cannot be talking about this case.

keyTerms.meaning: Separate bodies: different people involved in the sin
Separate 'names': separate prohibitions or separate titles of a sin
Widow, forbidden to a כהן גדול

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two ideas. 'Separate bodies' means different people. 'Separate names' means different prohibitions or titles. The end of this section depends on telling them apart.

phrases.english: Aren't they separate bodies,
phrases.notes: He means three different women. The גמרא just suggested that 'many widows' means three separate widows.

phrases.english: Aren't they separate names [of prohibition]!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי גּוּפִין מוּחְלָקִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the suggestion made just before this text: that 'many widows' means three different widows.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the ruling as three separate widows.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Separate bodies and separate prohibitions each bring a separate punishment, so three widows cannot mean only one punishment.

steps.title: New suggestion: one widow, three acts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the case is one widow with whom he had relations three times.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the case is that he was with one widow three times.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a new way to read the case. There is only one woman, but there are three separate acts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With one woman, there are no separate bodies and no separate names. The only thing that might split the punishment is the number of acts. The גמרא will now test this suggestion.

keyTerms.meaning: Acts of relations

phrases.english: Rather, that he had relations with one widow
three acts of relations.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא שֶׁבָּא עַל אַלְמָנָה אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected three-widows reading with a one-widow reading.
steps.terutzMaskana: Perhaps it means several acts with one widow.

steps.title: With only one warning, the ruling would be obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exactly the case is. If he was not warned before each act, then of course there is only one punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: What exactly is the case? If they did not warn him before each act, it is obvious that he gets only one punishment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks the new suggestion. If he was warned only once, the ruling 'only one punishment' teaches nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מלקות requires a warning before the sin (התראה). One warning covers only one punishment, so three acts after one warning obviously bring one set of מלקות. A ברייתא would not bother to teach something that obvious.

keyTerms.meaning: What are the circumstances? What exactly is the case?
They warned him (gave him התראה)
It is obvious, so why would it need to be taught?

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If they did not warn him –
phrases.notes: He means they did not warn him separately before each act. Without a warning, a person does not get מלקות.

phrases.english: it is obvious that he is liable only once.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָמֵי? אִי דְּלָא אַתְרוֹ בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the one-widow suggestion by asking about the warnings.
steps.kashyaTarget: The one-widow, three-acts reading, if there was only one warning.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With one warning the ruling is too obvious to need teaching.

steps.title: Maybe he was warned before each act
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries saying that he was warned separately before every act.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the case is that they warned him for each and every act.
steps.whatsHappening: To avoid the 'obvious' problem, the גמרא suggests that there was a separate warning before each act. This sets up the next challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If there was a warning before each act, then saying 'only one punishment' would be a real new teaching. But that raises a new problem, which the גמרא brings right away.

keyTerms.meaning: For each and every one

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא דְּאַתְרוֹ בֵּיהּ אַכֹּל חֲדָא וַחֲדָא –
phrases.english: Rather, that they warned him for each and every one –

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דְּאַתְרוֹ בֵּיהּ אַכֹּל חֲדָא וַחֲדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries a second version of the one-widow case to get around the 'obvious' problem.
steps.terutzMaskana: There was a separate warning before each act.

steps.title: The נזיר משנה: each warning brings its own punishment
steps.stepSummary: If he was warned each time, why only one punishment? The משנה about a נזיר says that each warned act brings its own מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then why is he liable only once? We learned in a משנה: a נזיר who drank wine all day is liable only once. But if they kept telling him 'Don't drink! Don't drink!' and he drank anyway, he is liable for each time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the 'warned each time' version by bringing a משנה about a נזיר. That משנה proves that separate warnings bring separate punishments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The נזיר case shows the rule. One long sin with one warning brings one punishment. Repeated warnings followed by repeated sins bring a punishment for each one. So a כהן גדול warned before each act should get three punishments, and this version of the case falls apart too.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who vowed to stay away from wine, among other things
Why?

steps.whatToRemember: Separate warnings make separate punishments, even for the same sin with the same object.

phrases.english: Why is he liable only once?
But didn't we learn in a משנה:
phrases.notes: This משנה is in מסכת נזיר, דף מב.

phrases.english: A נזיר who was drinking wine
the entire day –
is liable only once.
If they said to him: 'Do not drink! Do not drink!'
and he drinks anyway –
he is liable for each and every one!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמַּאי אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב אֶלָּא אַחַת? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Knocks down the 'warned each time' version using a משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The one-widow case with a warning before each act.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The נזיר משנה shows that repeated warnings bring repeated punishments, so this case would need three punishments, not one.

steps.title: One widow with three 'widow' names, one act
steps.stepSummary: The real case is one act with a woman who was widowed from ראובן, שמעון and לוי. Separate names alone are not enough; separate bodies are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the ruling is needed for a case where he was with ראובן's widow, who had also been שמעון's widow and לוי's widow. You might have thought these are separate names, so there should be three punishments. The ruling teaches us that we need separate bodies, and there are none here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final answer. The case is one act with one woman who carries three 'widow' titles, and the ruling teaches that this brings only one punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This case gets around every earlier problem. There is one body, one act and one warning, but there is still a real reason to think she counts three times, because she has three 'widow' titles. The ruling teaches that separate titles alone do not split the punishment; separate bodies are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for this case
You might have said / I might have thought
It teaches us (the new point)
We require

steps.whatToRemember: Separate bodies (different people) split the punishment. Several 'widow' titles on one woman do not. That is why 'many widows' brings only one set of מלקות.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that several titles on the same person or object are not automatically several sins. The real people or acts involved decide how many punishments there are.

phrases.english: No, it is needed,
where he had relations with ראובן's widow
who had been שמעון's widow
who had been לוי's widow.
You might have said
they are separate names –
so it teaches us
we require separate bodies, and there are none.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, שֶׁבָּא עַל אַלְמְנַת רְאוּבֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the one-widow, many-acts reading behind and gives the final case that avoids every challenge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Three 'widow' titles would bring three punishments.
steps.terutzMaskana: Separate bodies are needed, so there is only one punishment.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A כהן גדול who has relations once with a woman widowed several times gets only one set of מלקות, because she is only one body.

steps.title: Why does the order of the woman's statuses matter?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next case of the ברייתא (אלמנה, then גרושה, then חללה, then זונה) and asks what this תנא holds. Whichever view he holds, the order should not make a difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said: 'a widow, a divorcée, a חללה, a זונה' (in this order, he gets lashes for each). What does this תנא hold? If he holds that a prohibition takes effect on top of another prohibition, then the reverse order should also work! And if he holds that a prohibition does not take effect on top of another prohibition, then even in this order it should not work!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's case of a woman who became four forbidden types, one after another. It challenges why the ruling depends on the order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two basic views. In the first, a new prohibition can land on a woman who is already forbidden (איסור חל על איסור). In the second, it cannot. Under the first view, every order should bring extra מלקות. Under the second view, no order should. So neither view explains why only 'this order' works.

keyTerms.meaning: A prohibition takes effect on top of an existing prohibition
He holds (what is his opinion?)
The reverse, the opposite order
In this order

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not saying that some of these women are less forbidden. They are all forbidden to a כהן גדול. The question is only whether he gets extra sets of מלקות for one act.

phrases.english: 'A widow, and a divorcée, and a חללה, a זונה.'
What does this תנא hold?

phrases.aramaic: אִי קָסָבַר אִיסּוּר חָל עַל אִיסּוּר –
phrases.english: If he holds that a prohibition takes effect on top of a prohibition,
then the reverse order too!
phrases.notes: For example, if she was first a זונה and later a widow, he should still get lashes for each.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי קָסָבַר אֵין אִיסּוּר חָל עַל אִיסּוּר –
phrases.english: And if he holds that a prohibition does not take effect on top of a prohibition,
then even in this order, also not!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי תַּנָּא מַאי קָסָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling the case of one woman widowed three times, the גמרא moves to the ברייתא's next case: one woman with several different statuses.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that extra מלקות apply only when the statuses come in this specific order.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A dilemma. Under either view of איסור חל על איסור, the order should not matter. So the ברייתא's dependence on order has no clear basis.

steps.title: רבא: this תנא accepts an 'added prohibition'
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that this תנא rejects איסור חל על איסור in general, but he does accept איסור מוסיף, a new prohibition that adds a new restriction.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This תנא does not hold that a prohibition takes effect on top of a prohibition. But he does hold that an added prohibition takes effect.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the dilemma with a third option, a middle path between the two views.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In general, a second prohibition cannot land on a woman who is already forbidden. But if the new prohibition also makes her forbidden in a new way that did not exist before, it does take effect, even for the people she was already forbidden to. This explains why the order matters. Only an order where each step adds something new will work.

keyTerms.meaning: An added prohibition: a new prohibition that adds a new restriction beyond the old one
He does not hold of / he does hold of

steps.whyThisMatters: איסור מוסיף is a basic rule that shows up all over ש״ס, wherever the גמרא asks whether one prohibition can stack on another.

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: הַאי תַּנָּא אִיסּוּר חָל עַל אִיסּוּר לֵית לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: This תנא does not hold that a prohibition takes effect on top of a prohibition,
but he does hold of an added prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הַאי תַּנָּא אִיסּוּר חָל עַל אִיסּוּר לֵית לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the dilemma of step 7 by bringing a third principle.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a middle principle (איסור מוסיף) that gets out of the either-or dilemma.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The questioner thought the only choices were that prohibitions always stack, or that they never stack.
steps.terutzMaskana: Prohibitions do not usually stack, but a prohibition that adds a new restriction does take effect. So order matters.

steps.title: How each new status adds a new prohibition
steps.stepSummary: רבא walks through the order. אלמנה is forbidden only to a כהן גדול. גרושה adds a prohibition for a כהן הדיוט. חללה adds a prohibition on eating תרומה. Each new status adds something, so it also takes effect for the כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: A widow is forbidden to a כהן גדול and permitted to a regular כהן. Once she becomes a divorcée, a prohibition has been added for her toward a regular כהן. Because of that, a prohibition is also added toward a כהן גדול. But she is still allowed to eat תרומה. Once she becomes a חללה, a prohibition to eat תרומה has been added. Because of that, a prohibition is also added toward a כהן גדול.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains his rule by showing, step by step, how each new status adds a new restriction that did not exist before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key word is מיגו ('since'). Since the new status takes effect for a new restriction, it also takes effect for the כהן גדול, even though she was already forbidden to him. In the reverse order, a later status would add nothing new. For example, a חללה is already forbidden to all כהנים and to תרומה, so becoming a גרושה adds nothing. That is why only this order brings extra מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: Since (since it takes effect here, it takes effect there too)
A regular כהן, not the כהן גדול
A divorcée
A woman disqualified from כהונה, for example through a forbidden relationship with a כהן
The holy portion given to כהנים, which a כהן's daughter may eat

steps.confusionAlert: The new prohibition is not 'added' only for the new people. Through מיגו, it also takes effect for the כהן גדול, who was already forbidden to her. That is where the extra מלקות come from.

phrases.english: A widow is forbidden to a כהן גדול
and permitted to a regular כהן.
Once she becomes a divorcée,

phrases.aramaic: מִיגּוֹ דְּאִיתּוֹסַף לַהּ אִיסּוּרָא לְגַבֵּי כֹּהֵן הֶדְיוֹט –
phrases.english: since a prohibition was added for her toward a regular כהן,

phrases.aramaic: אִיתּוֹסַף לַהּ אִיסּוּרָא לְגַבֵּי כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל,
phrases.english: a prohibition is also added for her toward a כהן גדול,
and she is still permitted to eat תרומה.
Once she becomes a חללה,
since a prohibition to eat תרומה was added,
a prohibition is also added toward a כהן גדול.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָנָה אֲסוּרָה לְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל וְשַׁרְיָא לְכֹהֵן הֶדְיוֹט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's answer by applying the איסור מוסיף rule to each step in the ברייתא's order.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows how the principle works by going through the ברייתא's case step by step.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It was not yet clear what each status adds or why the order matters.
steps.terutzMaskana: אלמנה, then גרושה, then חללה: each one adds a new restriction, so each one takes effect for the כהן גדול too.

steps.title: What new prohibition does זונה add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא's explanation at its last step. A זונה is forbidden to the same people as a חללה, so what does זונה add?
steps.simpleTranslation: But a זונה: what added prohibition is there with her?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last item on the list. Becoming a זונה after being a חללה seems to add nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חללה is already forbidden to all כהנים and to תרומה. A זונה is forbidden to the same people. So under רבא's rule, the זונה prohibition should not take effect, yet the ברייתא gives מלקות for it too.

keyTerms.meaning: In כהונה law: a woman forbidden to a כהן because of a forbidden relationship

phrases.english: But a זונה:
what added prohibition is there with her?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא זוֹנָה מַאי אִיסּוּר מוֹסִיף אִית בַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests רבא's rule on the last item of the ברייתא's list.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's explanation that each status in the ברייתא is an איסור מוסיף.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: זונה adds no new restriction beyond חללה. So by רבא's own rule, it should not bring extra מלקות.

steps.title: The label זנות can disqualify even for a ישראל
steps.stepSummary: רב חנא בר רב קטינא answers that זונה does add something. The label of זנות can make a woman forbidden even to a regular ישראל, which a חללה status never does.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנא בר רב קטינא said: Since the label of זנות disqualifies a woman even for a ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חנא בר רב קטינא answers the challenge by showing a new restriction that comes with the name זנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being a חללה matters only for כהנים and תרומה. The broader idea of זנות, such as a married woman who is unfaithful, can make her forbidden to her ישראל husband. Because the label זנות reaches further than חללה, it counts as an איסור מוסיף, and רבא's rule still holds.

keyTerms.meaning: The label or category of זנות (forbidden relations)
Disqualifies, makes forbidden
Since, because

steps.whatToRemember: This תנא does not let prohibitions stack in general. A new status takes effect only if it adds a new restriction (איסור מוסיף). אלמנה, then גרושה, then חללה, then זונה is an order where each step adds something, and זונה adds because זנות can disqualify even for a ישראל.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חָנָא בַּר רַב קַטִּינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Chana bar Rav Ketina said:
Since the label of זנות disqualifies among ישראל.
phrases.notes: He means that זנות can make a woman forbidden even to a non-כהן, like her own husband, something a חללה status never does.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חָנָא בַּר רַב קַטִּינָא: הוֹאִיל וְשֵׁם זְנוּת פּוֹסֵל בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10 and saves רבא's איסור מוסיף explanation.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a wider scope of the category זנות, which makes it count as an added prohibition.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: זונה seemed to add nothing beyond חללה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The label זנות reaches further, even to a ישראל, so it is an איסור מוסיף and brings its own מלקות.

steps.title: A ברייתא about the כהן גדול and his widowed sister
steps.stepSummary: A תנא recites a ברייתא before רב ששת. Only a woman the כהן גדול could otherwise marry is included in the לאו of marrying an אלמנה. This leaves out his widowed sister.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא taught before רב ששת: Any woman who is included in 'he shall take' is included in 'he shall not take.' Any woman who is not included in 'he shall take' is not included in 'he shall not take.' This excludes a כהן גדול who had relations with his widowed sister.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that was taught in front of רב ששת. The ברייתא says the לאו against a כהן גדול marrying an אלמנה only covers women he could otherwise marry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק tells the כהן גדול which women he 'shall not take' and which he 'shall take.' The ברייתא links the two halves: the 'do not take' only covers women who could be in the 'take' group. His sister is forbidden to him no matter what, so the לאו of אלמנה does not apply to her.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He shall take': the command for the כהן גדול to marry a בתולה
'He shall not take': the לאו against marrying an אלמנה, גרושה, חללה, or זונה
This excludes; it comes to leave out a certain case
His sister

phrases.english: A tanna taught before Rav Sheshet:
phrases.notes: A תנא here is someone whose job was to memorize and recite ברייתות.

phrases.english: Any woman who is included in "he shall take,"
is included in "he shall not take."
Any woman who is not included in "he shall take"
is not included in "he shall not take" –
this excludes a High Priest
who had relations with his widowed sister.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי תַּנָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב שֵׁשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new ברייתא that again deals with whether one prohibition can take effect on top of another, the topic of steps 7-11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן גדול does not violate the לאו of אלמנה with his widowed sister, because she was never a woman he could marry.

steps.title: רב ששת says the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת identifies the author of the ברייתא as רבי שמעון, who holds that a prohibition cannot take effect on top of an existing prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The one who told you this, whose view is it? It is רבי שמעון, who says: a prohibition does not take effect on top of another prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת tells the תנא whose view this ברייתא follows: רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sister is already forbidden to the כהן גדול as an ערוה. For רבי שמעון, once something is already forbidden, a new prohibition such as אלמנה cannot be added on top. That explains why the ברייתא says he does not violate the לאו of אלמנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is this? The standard way the גמרא asks who the author of a source is
A prohibition does not take effect where another prohibition already exists

phrases.english: He said to him: The one who told you this,
phrases.notes: רב ששת is speaking to the תנא who just recited the ברייתא.

phrases.english: whose view is it? It is Rabbi Shimon,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: אֵין אִיסּוּר חָל עַל אִיסּוּר.
phrases.english: who says: A prohibition does not take effect on top of another prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: דַּאֲמַר לָךְ, מַנִּי – רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains which Tanna's principle stands behind the ruling of the ברייתא in step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whose view does the ברייתא follow?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי שמעון, who holds אין איסור חל על איסור.

steps.title: Proof of רבי שמעון's view from נבילה on יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת backs up his claim with a ברייתא. There רבי שמעון exempts someone who eats נבילה on יום הכפורים. He adds that the רבנן disagree, so the ברייתא of step 12 cannot be theirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: רבי שמעון says: One who eats נבילה on יום הכפורים is exempt. For if it were the רבנן, they say: a prohibition does take effect on top of another prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת quotes a source showing that רבי שמעון really holds this principle. He also explains why the ברייתא cannot follow the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The meat was already forbidden as נבילה before יום הכפורים began. רבי שמעון says the יום הכפורים prohibition does not take hold on it, so the person is exempt from the יום הכפורים punishment. The רבנן hold that the second prohibition does take effect, so according to רב ששת they would also make the כהן גדול liable for אלמנה.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that died without proper שחיטה, which is forbidden to eat
The fast day, when eating is forbidden
Exempt from punishment
For if; introduces the reason another option does not work

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Shimon says:
One who eats a carcass on Yom Kippur is exempt.
phrases.notes: He means exempt from the יום הכפורים punishment, since the נבילה prohibition was there first.

phrases.english: For if it were the Rabbis,

phrases.aramaic: הָא אָמְרִי: אִיסּוּר חָל עַל אִיסּוּר.
phrases.english: don't they say: A prohibition does take effect on top of another prohibition?

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 13's claim by showing רבי שמעון holds אין איסור חל על איסור, and rules out the רבנן.
steps.raayaObject: That the ברייתא of step 12 must follow רבי שמעון.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא in which רבי שמעון exempts one who eats נבילה on יום הכפורים, against the רבנן who hold איסור חל על איסור.

steps.title: The ברייתא could follow the רבנן too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on רב ששת. Even the רבנן only say a severe prohibition takes effect on a light one. A light prohibition cannot take effect on a severe one, so the ברייתא fits them as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say it is the רבנן. When the רבנן say a prohibition takes effect on another prohibition, that is only a severe prohibition on a light one. But a light prohibition on a severe one does not take effect.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the idea that only רבי שמעון can hold this ברייתא. It shows that the רבנן could agree with it too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן's rule has a limit: a stronger prohibition can land on a weaker one, but not the other way around. The sister prohibition is the severe one, and the אלמנה prohibition is the light one. So even for the רבנן, אלמנה cannot be added on top of the sister prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say; shows a source can fit the other opinion too
This applies only; introduces a limit on a rule
A severe prohibition
A light prohibition
Does not take effect

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up which prohibition is which here. The sister is the severe prohibition that was already there. The אלמנה status is the light one trying to come on top, so it cannot take effect.

phrases.english: You can even say it is the Rabbis,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אָמְרִי רַבָּנַן אִיסּוּר חָל עַל אִיסּוּר –
phrases.english: when the Rabbis say a prohibition takes effect on top of another prohibition –

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי מִילֵּי אִיסּוּר חָמוּר עַל אִיסּוּר קַל,
phrases.english: that applies only to a severe prohibition on top of a light prohibition,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אִיסּוּר קַל עַל אִיסּוּר חָמוּר – לָא חָיֵיל.
phrases.english: but a light prohibition on top of a severe prohibition does not take effect.
phrases.notes: Here the sister is the severe prohibition and אלמנה is the light one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the conclusion of steps 13-14 that the ברייתא must be רבי שמעון.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the claim that the ברייתא must follow רבי שמעון. It does not deny that רבי שמעון could also hold it.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב ששת assumed the רבנן say any prohibition takes effect on another. In fact they only say this for a severe prohibition on a light one.

steps.title: Second version: רב ששת said the ברייתא is the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: In a second version of the story, רב ששת himself says the ברייתא follows the רבנן. They hold a severe prohibition takes effect on a light one, but a light one does not take effect on a severe one.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are those who say: Whose view is this? It is the רבנן, who say a prohibition takes effect on another prohibition. And when the רבנן say this, it is only a severe prohibition on a light one, but a light prohibition on a severe one does not take effect.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another version of what רב ששת told the תנא. In this version he names the רבנן as the author from the start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This version uses the same limit on the רבנן's rule that step 15 used. Here it is not a rejection of anything; it is רב ששת's own first answer. The proof of why it cannot be רבי שמעון comes in the next step.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
Whose view is this? It is the Rabbis,
who say: A prohibition takes effect on top of another prohibition,

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי אָמְרִי רַבָּנַן אִיסּוּר חָל עַל אִיסּוּר,
phrases.english: and when the Rabbis say a prohibition takes effect on top of another prohibition,

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי מִילֵּי אִיסּוּר חָמוּר עַל אִיסּוּר קַל,
phrases.english: that applies only to a severe prohibition on top of a light prohibition,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אִיסּוּר קַל עַל אִיסּוּר חָמוּר – לָא חָיֵיל.
phrases.english: but a light prohibition on top of a severe prohibition does not take effect.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי: הָא מַנִּי – רַבָּנַן הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second version of רב ששת's answer to step 12. This time he names the רבנן instead of רבי שמעון.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying the author of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: In the first version, the ברייתא was thought to be only רבי שמעון.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is the רבנן: a light prohibition (אלמנה) does not take effect on a severe one (sister).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the second version, רב ששת says the ברייתא follows the רבנן. They hold that a severe prohibition takes effect on a light one, but a light prohibition (אלמנה) does not take effect on a severe one (his sister).

steps.title: Why the ברייתא cannot be רבי שמעון in this version
steps.stepSummary: In this second version, the ברייתא cannot follow רבי שמעון. For him even a severe prohibition does not take effect on a light one, so teaching that a light one does not take effect on a severe one would be obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if it were רבי שמעון: now that a severe prohibition does not take effect on a light one, is it even necessary to say that a light prohibition does not take effect on a severe one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why, in this second version, רב ששת did not say the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון does not let even a stronger prohibition land on a weaker one. So of course a weaker one cannot land on a stronger one, and the ברייתא would be teaching something obvious. A ברייתא should teach something new, so it must follow the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Now that; begins an 'all the more so' argument
Is it necessary to say? Meaning it is obvious

steps.whatToRemember: Both versions agree on the ruling: the כהן גדול is not liable for אלמנה with his widowed sister. They differ only on who the author is. Version one says רבי שמעון, and the גמרא adds that it could also be the רבנן. Version two says the רבנן, because for רבי שמעון the ruling would seem too obvious. The next step shows it is not obvious even for רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: For if it were Rabbi Shimon,

phrases.aramaic: הַשְׁתָּא אִיסּוּר חָמוּר עַל אִיסּוּר קַל לָא חָיֵיל,
phrases.english: now that even a severe prohibition on top of a light prohibition does not take effect,

phrases.aramaic: אִיסּוּר קַל עַל אִיסּוּר חָמוּר מִיבַּעְיָא?
phrases.english: is it necessary to say that a light prohibition on top of a severe prohibition does not?

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, הַשְׁתָּא אִיסּוּר חָמוּר עַל אִיסּוּר קַל לָא חָיֵיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for step 16's choice of the רבנן by ruling out רבי שמעון.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי שמעון as the author of the ברייתא within the second version.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: For רבי שמעון the ruling would be obvious from a קל וחומר, so the ברייתא would have no reason to teach it.

steps.title: Why the teaching is still needed for רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is not obvious for רבי שמעון. We might have thought that prohibitions of כהונה are an exception, so it had to teach us otherwise.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that a prohibition of כהונה is different. So it teaches us that it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the claim from the last step that the ברייתא would be 'obvious' for רבי שמעון. It explains why the ברייתא still needed to say it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 said: for רבי שמעון, no prohibition ever takes effect on another, so there is nothing new to teach. The answer is that we might have thought כהונה prohibitions are special and do stack up. The ברייתא tells us that even there, a second prohibition does not take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (a mistaken idea the teaching comes to correct)
A prohibition that applies specifically to כהנים
Is different
It teaches us (that this is not so)

steps.whatToRemember: In this version, the ברייתא can fit רבי שמעון after all. Its new point is that even prohibitions of כהונה do not take effect on top of an existing prohibition.

phrases.english: You might have said:
a prohibition of the priesthood is different,
so it teaches us that it is not.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: אִיסּוּר כְּהוּנָּה שָׁאנֵי, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'it's obvious' argument of step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: shows the teaching was needed to block a mistaken idea
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Prohibitions of כהונה are stricter, so they might take effect on top of an existing prohibition
steps.terutzMaskana: Even for prohibitions of כהונה, רבי שמעון holds that a second prohibition does not take effect

steps.title: Does a sister who lived with her brother become a חללה?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks אביי about a sister who lived with her brother. She becomes a זונה, but does she also become a חללה? The question has two sides: a קל וחומר from ordinary prohibitions, or perhaps only a prohibition of כהונה makes a חללה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: When a ישראל lives with his sister, that makes her a זונה. Does it also make her a חללה, or not? Do we say a קל וחומר: if a woman becomes a חללה through a relationship that is only a regular לאו, then surely she becomes one through a relationship punished by כרת? Or maybe a woman becomes a חללה only through a prohibition of כהונה?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב פפא asks whether a forbidden relationship with a close relative also gives the woman the status of חללה, and lays out both sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees she becomes a זונה, which already forbids her to a כהן. The question is whether she is also a חללה. If so, a כהן who lives with her would break a second, separate prohibition. One side is a קל וחומר: a lighter sin (a לאו) can make a חללה, so a heavier sin (כרת) surely should. The other side is that חללה status comes only from a prohibition of כהונה.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman forbidden to a כהן because of a forbidden relationship
A woman who loses the right to marry a כהן, usually through a relationship forbidden by the rules of כהונה
A logical argument from a lighter case to a stricter one
Relationships forbidden by a regular negative commandment
Relationships punished by כרת, which are more severe
Makes her (into that status)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
An Israelite who lives with his sister –
makes her a zona.
Does he make her a ḥalala
or does he not make her one?
Do we say a kal vachomer:
from relationships forbidden by a regular prohibition she becomes a ḥalala,
so from relationships punished by karet, all the more so?
Or perhaps a woman is not a ḥalala
except through a prohibition of the priesthood?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question, related in theme to prohibitions of כהונה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a relationship punished by כרת, which is not a prohibition of כהונה, make a woman a חללה?

steps.title: אביי: only a prohibition of כהונה makes a חללה
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that a woman becomes a חללה only through a prohibition of כהונה. So the sister is a זונה but not a חללה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: A woman becomes a חללה only through a prohibition of כהונה, and nothing else.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רב פפא's question. He rejects the קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though כרת is more severe, it does not create חללה status. חללה status is not about how severe the sin is. It is tied only to the special prohibitions of כהונה, so the קל וחומר does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: Only, and nothing else

phrases.english: He said to him:
a ḥalala comes about
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets. Either way, the meaning is the same.

phrases.english: only through a prohibition of the priesthood, and nothing else.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֵין (אִיסּוּר) חֲלָלָה אֶלָּא מֵאִיסּוּר כְּהוּנָּה בִּלְבַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A sister who lived with her brother is not a חללה, because only a prohibition of כהונה creates חללה status
steps.whatToRemember: חללה status comes only from a prohibition of כהונה, not from other sins, however severe.

steps.title: רבא asks for the source of אביי's rule
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks where we learn the rule that a woman becomes a חללה only through a prohibition of כהונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: From where do we know what the רבנן said, that a woman becomes a חללה only through a prohibition of כהונה?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks for the source of the rule just stated. This sets up the next step, where he brings a ברייתא as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is being challenged here. The rule is accepted, and רבא wants to show where it comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: From where is this matter learned?

phrases.english: Rava says:
From where is this matter
that the Sages said:
"A ḥalala comes about only through a prohibition of the priesthood"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנָא הָא מִילְּתָא דַּאֲמוּר רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the answer in step 20
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that only a prohibition of כהונה creates חללה status

steps.title: The ברייתא about a גרושה and a כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a ברייתא. The Torah did not need to forbid a גרושה to a כהן גדול, since a קל וחומר from a regular כהן would teach it. It says it anyway to teach that, just as for a regular כהן, the prohibition of גרושה is separate from זונה and חללה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: The Torah did not need to say that a גרושה is forbidden to a כהן גדול. We could learn it with a קל וחומר from a regular כהן: if she is forbidden even to a regular כהן, surely she is forbidden to a כהן גדול! So why is it written? To teach that just as for a regular כהן the prohibition of a גרושה is separate from that of a זונה and a חללה, so too for a כהן גדול it is separate.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a ברייתא as the source for the rule. The ברייתא explains why a verse that seems extra is really needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first claims the verse is extra, because a קל וחומר from a regular כהן would teach it. It answers that the verse is there to make the prohibition of גרושה a separate one for a כהן גדול too, so he can be punished for it on its own, apart from זונה and חללה. The line that actually proves only a prohibition of כהונה makes a חללה comes later in this same ברייתא, in step 25.

keyTerms.meaning: A divorced woman, forbidden to a כהן
The High Priest
A regular כהן
Separate, a distinct prohibition with its own punishment
Does it even need to be said?

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא does not say that a גרושה is permitted to a כהן גדול without the verse. The verse is needed only to make her prohibition a separate, extra one.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
The verse need not state that a divorcée is forbidden to a High Priest,
phrases.notes: The verse about the כהן גדול is ויקרא 21:14.

phrases.english: and one could derive it by a kal vachomer from a common priest,
as I would say:
Now, if she is forbidden to a common priest,
does it even need to be said for a High Priest?
Why then is it stated?
Just as a divorcée is separate
from a zona and a ḥalala for a common priest,
so too it is separate for a High Priest.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: לֹא יֵאָמֵר גְּרוּשָׁה בְּכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source רבא asked for in step 21
steps.raayaObject: The rule that only a prohibition of כהונה makes a woman a חללה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא explaining that the verse forbidding a גרושה to a כהן גדול makes it a prohibition separate from זונה and חללה
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the base text for רבא's proof. The connection to חללה status is worked out from it next.

steps.title: Why would a High Priest's rules be any weaker?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the ברייתא's lesson is obvious. A כהן גדול keeps all the prohibitions he had as a regular כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is obvious! Did he become lower?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the wording of the ברייתא from Step 22. It asks why we would need a teaching that גרושה is a separate prohibition for a כהן גדול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said that for a כהן גדול, גרושה is separate from זונה and חללה, just as it is for a regular כהן. But a כהן גדול was a regular כהן first, and becoming כהן גדול only adds rules. It does not take any away, so the ברייתא seems to teach nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious
Did she (his status) become lower? Has it gone down?

phrases.english: It is obvious! Has his status become lower?

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא, מִיגְרָע גָּרְעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the ברייתא quoted in Step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that, for a כהן גדול, the prohibition of גרושה is separate from זונה and חללה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A כהן גדול never loses the prohibitions of a regular כהן, so this lesson is too obvious to need teaching.

steps.title: Reword the ברייתא to be about אלמנה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is reworded. For a כהן גדול, אלמנה is a separate prohibition from גרושה, חללה and זונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say it this way: just as for a regular כהן, גרושה is a separate prohibition from זונה and חללה, so too for a כהן גדול, אלמנה is separate from גרושה, חללה and זונה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording of the ברייתא. The real lesson is about אלמנה, which is forbidden only to a כהן גדול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אלמנה is a new prohibition that only a כהן גדול has, so it does need teaching. The point is that a כהן גדול who marries a woman who is an אלמנה, a גרושה, a חללה and a זונה breaks each prohibition separately, even though they all appear in one פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Separate, counted as its own prohibition
A widow, forbidden to a כהן גדול
A regular כהן, not the כהן גדול

phrases.english: Rather: just as a divorcée is separate
from a זונה and a חללה for a common priest –
so too a widow is separate
from a divorcée, a חללה, and a זונה
for a High Priest.
phrases.notes: All four women are listed together in one פסוק, ויקרא 21:14.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 23 by rewording the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to teach the obvious point that גרושה stays separate for a כהן גדול.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא teaches that אלמנה, a prohibition only for a כהן גדול, counts separately from the others.

steps.title: A חללה comes only from a prohibition of כהונה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks why חללה is repeated for a כהן גדול. It answers that a woman becomes a חללה only through a prohibition of כהונה. This is רבא's source.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why was חללה said again? To teach that a woman becomes a חללה only through a prohibition of כהונה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and reaches the line רבא needs. It proves the rule from Step 21: a woman becomes a חללה only through a prohibition of כהונה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חללה is already forbidden to every כהן, so repeating her for a כהן גדול must teach something. The ברייתא does not spell out how the repetition teaches its lesson. It simply states the lesson: a woman becomes a חללה only through a prohibition of כהונה. This backs up אביי's answer in Step 20 that the sister is not a חללה.

keyTerms.meaning: Why was it said? (Why does the פסוק need it?)
A prohibition that applies specifically to כהנים

steps.whyThisMatters: This line is the source for the rule אביי gave and רבא asked about. An ordinary forbidden relationship can make a woman a זונה, but not a חללה.

phrases.english: Why was חללה stated?
A חללה results only from a prohibition of priesthood.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲלָלָה לָמָּה נֶאֶמְרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא and gives the exact proof רבא was looking for.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a woman becomes a חללה only through a prohibition of כהונה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's explanation of why חללה is repeated for a כהן גדול (ויקרא 21:14).

steps.title: Why זונה is repeated: a regular כהן's children also become חללים
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains the repetition of זונה with a גזירה שוה. A regular כהן who lives with a זונה also makes his children חללים, just like a כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why was זונה said again? It says זונה here (כהן גדול) and זונה there (regular כהן). Just as here his children are profaned, so too there his children are profaned.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes by explaining the repetition of זונה. It links the two פסוקים that both say the word זונה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a כהן גדול, the פסוק right afterward says his children become profaned. Because the same word זונה appears for both, that result carries over to a regular כהן. So a regular כהן who lives with a זונה also makes his children חללים.

keyTerms.meaning: Here... there: linking two פסוקים by a shared word
His children are profaned (they become חללים)
A woman forbidden to a כהן because of a forbidden relationship

phrases.english: Why was זונה stated?
It is stated here: "זונה",
phrases.notes: "Here" is the כהן גדול's פסוק, ויקרא 21:14.

phrases.english: and it is stated there: "זונה",
phrases.notes: "There" is the regular כהן's פסוק, ויקרא 21:7.

phrases.english: just as here his offspring are profaned,
so too there his offspring are profaned.

steps.triggerLanguage: זוֹנָה לָמָּה נֶאֶמְרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with its next question, this time about זונה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A regular כהן who lives with a זונה makes his children חללים, learned by a shared-word link from the כהן גדול.

steps.title: רב אשי begins a practical result: a כהן with his sister
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי starts to apply the rules just learned to a כהן who lives with his sister. His statement continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Therefore, a כהן who lives with his sister...
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי begins to draw a practical result from the ברייתא. The sentence is cut off here, so this line is setting up a ruling that finishes in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "therefore" shows that רב אשי is building on what was just taught. That includes the rule that a חללה comes only from a prohibition of כהונה, and the rule about a זונה. He is now applying these to the case of a כהן with his sister, which ties back to רב פפא's question in Step 19.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore, as a result
Who lives with his sister

phrases.english: Rav Ashi says:
Consequently, a priest who engages in intercourse with his sister
phrases.notes: His sentence continues on the next amud, where he tells us the result.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: הִילְכָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a practical result from the ברייתא that was just finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Opening of רב אשי's ruling about a כהן who lives with his sister. The ruling itself continues in the next section.
